mem-back-mechanic-ch15-rule6-content.title: Back Mechanic chapter 15 (Rule #6) source content saved for new book continuation
mem-back-mechanic-ch15-rule6-content.content: Chapter 15 of 'The Back Mechanic' by Stuart McGill covers Rule #6, 'Crawl Before You Walk, Walk Before You Run': progressive movement retraining is essential for permanent back-pain relief, and each level should be mastered before advancing. Key teachings: (1) 'Be still to heal' (Rule #2) becomes a daily-life habit of moving with a relatively still lumbar spine; (2) progression sequence: neutral-spine marching in place (the 'crawl' stage) then walking with neutral spine (stand tall, use the core to lock the neutral spine, swing arms from the shoulders opposite to the legs, take sitting breaks when pain approaches) then hip-hinge (axis of movement at the hips, not the low back; lumbar spine stays neutral and protected) then full-body rotation (chest, navel, and hips move together via hips, knees, and pelvis; rib cage stays locked to the pelvis) then torso rotation combining hip-hinge and squat for everyday tasks like unloading a dishwasher; (3) troubleshooting: if any movement hurts, regress to the last pain-free step (e.g., marching in place) for a few days before progressing again; knee pain means pivot the feet or drop into a catcher-style squat; back pain likely means twisting at the waist, rounding the back, or insufficient glute strength. The user sent this full chapter text on 2023-05-20 and explicitly asked to keep it in memory as source material.
